forces.title: Strengthening construction activity across commercial and civil engineering
forces.description: Construction activity in Ireland continues to strengthen, with broad-based growth. Commercial construction is seeing the strongest gains, and civil engineering activity has reached its highest level since 2022. This expansion in overall construction projects indicates a robust demand environment for Construction Materials, supporting volumes and sales in the near to medium term.

forces.title: Housing segment weak due to policy constraints on investment
forces.description: The housing segment remains the weakest-performing area within Irish construction, primarily due to taxation and rent-cap policies that have constrained investment. Despite strong underlying demand, this weakness limits growth potential for residential-focused Construction Materials, posing a challenge for businesses heavily reliant on the housing market.

forces.title: Cost inflation, staff shortages, and lengthening delivery times persist
forces.description: The Irish construction sector faces persistent challenges from cost inflation, staff shortages, and lengthening delivery times across the supply chain. These factors increase operational costs for Construction Materials producers and distributors, compress margins, and complicate project scheduling, necessitating robust financial discipline and supply chain management to mitigate risks.

forces.title: AI adoption transforming workflows and boosting productivity in construction
forces.description: The Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) sector, including Building Materials, is undergoing a structural change due to AI adoption. AI agents are being embedded across the project lifecycle, automating routine tasks and enabling human experts to focus on complex decisions. This shift is expected to significantly improve productivity, efficiency, and consistency, reshaping how work is done from design to field execution.
forces.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

forces.title: New commercial models focusing on outcomes, not just hours
forces.description: The advent of AI allows AEC firms to shift from charging based on labor hours to outcome-based models, such as fixed fees, milestone payments, or shared savings. This transformation in commercial models could enable Construction Materials firms to capture greater value from productivity gains, by selling 'excellence' and reliable project outcomes rather than just material inputs, enhancing profitability.
forces.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

forces.title: M&A in building products driven by strategic shifts and new categories
forces.description: Dealmaking in the building products sector is increasingly characterized by scope deals, where companies pursue new markets, customer segments, and channels. This strategic shift reflects a desire to reinvent businesses and access higher-margin segments, as exemplified by James Hardie's acquisition of Azek for exterior and decking products. This indicates a focus on portfolio transformation and capability acquisition within Construction Materials.

forces.title: European construction sector forecast to return to growth
forces.description: After a period of decline and stagnation in 2024 and 2025 respectively, the European construction sector is projected to grow by 1.5% in 2026. This recovery, supported by improving contractor confidence and increasing housing permits, creates a favorable demand environment for Construction Materials, indicating a positive shift in market conditions.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Building material costs largely stopped rising, easing pressure
forces.description: Building material costs have largely stopped rising, according to reports from early 2026. This stabilization or potential reduction in input costs is a significant relief for Construction Materials producers and distributors, alleviating margin pressure and making new construction projects more attractive. This cyclical shift enhances profitability and encourages investment in new builds.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: EU Affordable Housing Plan to boost new home construction
forces.description: The European Affordable Housing Plan, published in December 2025, aims to add 650,000 extra homes annually across the EU. This ambitious target, combined with efforts to streamline construction rules and promote sustainable, energy-efficient housing, presents a substantial long-term demand driver and upside opportunity for Construction Materials manufacturers and suppliers.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Focus on sustainable materials and innovative construction methods
forces.description: The European Strategy for Housing Construction emphasizes boosting innovation and the use of sustainable materials, alongside simplifying and digitalizing permitting procedures. This structural shift towards modern, eco-friendly construction methods will drive demand for new types of Construction Materials, rewarding firms that invest in R&D and adapt their product offerings to meet evolving standards.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Public investments in healthcare and education buildings
forces.description: Public investments in healthcare and educational buildings are providing positive counterforces in the non-residential construction sector. These sustained investments contribute to overall construction output and thus support demand for Construction Materials, offering stability in diverse sub-markets amidst varying conditions in other non-residential segments like offices.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Growth in infrastructure sector driven by energy transition
forces.description: The infrastructure sector demonstrates greater resilience and is experiencing growth due to essential investments in the energy transition, particularly new power grids and digital infrastructure. This ongoing investment directly fuels demand for specific Construction Materials used in large-scale infrastructure projects, contributing to a stable and growing market segment.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Scale premium shifting to procurement and pricing technology
forces.description: The building materials industry is experiencing a structural shift where scale advantages are moving from large production plants to advanced procurement and pricing technologies. The new 'scale premium' is now anchored by data visibility, digital quoting, and dynamic pricing capabilities, pushing companies to invest in technological solutions to maintain competitiveness and profitability, rather than solely relying on production capacity.
forces.source_title: Building materials: Understanding the keys to outperformance

viewpoints.title: Irish construction shows momentum, but housing remains weakest segment
viewpoints.description: Ireland's construction sector continues to strengthen, with growth across commercial and civil engineering activities, reaching its highest level since 2022. However, housing remains the weakest segment due to taxation and rent-cap policies, despite strong underlying demand. The sector generally exhibits healthy cash positions and low debt, but cost inflation, staff shortages, and lengthening delivery times pose ongoing risks, requiring financial discipline to sustain recovery.

viewpoints.title: AI adoption can unlock significant value for construction and building materials
viewpoints.description: The AEC (Architecture, Engineering, and Construction) industry, including Building Materials, is poised for significant value creation through AI. Early adopters are already seeing productivity gains in design, modeling, and construction-feasibility workflows. McKinsey projects AI could unlock approximately $126 billion in annual value in Europe's construction sector alone by 2030, by automating nonphysical work and improving consistency and efficiency across project lifecycles.
viewpoints.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

viewpoints.title: European building materials underperform when subscale and fragmented
viewpoints.description: The European building materials market generally underperforms compared to its North American counterpart, particularly when players are subscale or fragmented. This suggests that scale, operational model, and capital deployment are critical drivers of value creation (TSR) within product categories, rather than just market exposure. Despite this, premium European models still demonstrate success, indicating that strategic positioning and efficiency can overcome regional challenges.
viewpoints.source_title: Building materials: Understanding the keys to outperformance

viewpoints.title: European construction sector set for renewed growth in 2026 after stagnation
viewpoints.description: After a challenging period with declines in 2024 and stagnation in 2025, the European construction sector is expected to return to growth in 2026, with production increasing by 1.5%. Contractor confidence is improving, and new housing permits are on the rise. While the building sector previously suffered, infrastructure investment and renovation works, driven by EU funds and sustainability, are providing counterbalance and supporting the overall recovery.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: French construction faces low growth despite slight housing permit improvement
viewpoints.description: The French construction sector is forecast for only 0.5% growth in 2026, following a 1.5% decline in 2025. While housing permits saw a slight improvement early in 2025, they have declined since August, and contractor confidence remains low. This subdued outlook is linked to weak GDP growth, suggesting persistent challenges for the sector in France, despite minor positive signals in certain areas.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: Dutch building volumes face chronic bottlenecks despite modest growth
viewpoints.description: The Dutch building sector is expected to see only 0.5% growth in both 2025 and 2026, following a 2.9% contraction in 2024. Housing construction is particularly weak due to chronic bottlenecks including land shortages, complex permitting, grid congestion, and the country-specific nitrogen emission issue. These factors lead to project postponements and cancellations, significantly hindering recovery and growth prospects for construction materials demand.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: German construction projected to rebound in 2026 after prolonged decline
viewpoints.description: After five years of decline, the German construction industry, Europe's largest, is projected to return to growth in 2026 with an anticipated 2.5% growth rate. This recovery is driven by a gradual rebound in the new residential market and increased infrastructure investment. Government initiatives like 'housing construction turbo' aim to expedite planning and authorization, fostering optimism despite previous bureaucratic hurdles and a significant contraction between 2020-2025.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: Spanish construction shows strong recovery with positive growth outlook
viewpoints.description: The Spanish construction sector, after a significant decline between 2019 and 2022, has been recovering strongly since 2023, with a forecast of 2.5% growth in 2026. This positive outlook is supported by a surge in issued building permits, strong contractor confidence, and robust GDP growth. These factors indicate a healthy and sustained rebound, creating favorable conditions for construction materials demand.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: Belgian building permits decline despite VAT incentive for reconstruction
viewpoints.description: Belgium is one of the few European countries still facing a decline in issued building permits, attributed to time-consuming project procedures. Despite a reduced VAT rate of 6% for demolition and reconstruction, which aims to incentivize new builds, the overall decline persists. This indicates significant hurdles in stimulating new construction activity, leading to a cautious outlook for construction materials demand in the country.
viewpoints.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

viewpoints.title: Building materials industry delivered strong financial performance post-2015
viewpoints.description: The building materials industry in North America and Europe performed strongly from 2015 to 2024, achieving a solid CAGR of 12-13 percent in Total Shareholder Return (TSR). This success was driven by an increase in new builds, renovations, and higher prices following supply chain disruptions in 2021. The performance spread within product categories, driven by operating models and capital deployment, often exceeded the spread between categories, highlighting execution's importance.
viewpoints.source_title: Building materials: Understanding the keys to outperformance
